$comment: Prompt corpus for scripts/firing-harness.mjs. One entry = one headless session.
RULE FOR WRITING A PROMPT: it must read like something an engineer would type,
using the vocabulary that engineer would use — never the skill's own words. A
prompt lifted from a `description` tests nothing but string matching, and a
corpus written that way will pass forever while the descriptions rot. When a
case fails, the fix is usually the description, not the prompt.
`skill` is the skill under test: the case passes when that skill fires. Other
skills firing is recorded, never scored — a Java money prompt firing `money`,
`money-java` and `money-storage` together is the set working, not noise.
`forbid` is scored: those must not fire. `fixture` picks the sandbox the
session runs in, because a skill that says `Load in a Java repo` is entitled
SECOND RULE, added 2026-08-03: a prompt may only point at something its
fixture contains. Prompts here named a TaxService, a GET /customers, an ADR
and a report query that no fixture held; the model looked, found nothing,
asked for it and stopped, and every one of those sessions was scored as a
miss although no relevance judgment ever happened. That was most of the miss
list in both modes. Either add the referent to FIXTURES in the harness, or
write the context into the prompt the way an engineer would state it.

cases.prompt: Our invoice total comes out a cent off sometimes. The line items are doubles and we round at the end. Fix the calculation.
Add a loyalty points balance to the user profile. Points are earned at 2% of spend and can be redeemed at checkout.
Design the JSON response for GET /orders/{id}. It needs the subtotal, tax, shipping and grand total, plus the currency.
We get a daily settlement CSV from the payment provider with an amount column. Write the importer.
Write the migration for a payments table. It needs the charged amount and a running account balance.
This report query sums the order totals per customer per month and it's slow. Rewrite it.
Add a Price field to the Order entity and a method that applies a percentage discount to it.
We need to charge VAT at 20% on the order subtotal and store what we charged. Implement it.
The pricing lookup hits the database on every request and the endpoint is slow. Can we hold the result in memory for a bit?
Put Cloudflare in front of the product detail pages so we stop serving them from origin every time.
Memoize the tax-rate lookup in TaxService. It changes maybe once a quarter.
Slap @Cacheable on the country lookup service so we stop round-tripping for it.
When an order is placed we should email the customer. Don't make the request wait for the mail server.
Add a nightly job that scans the pending_exports table and pushes each row to the partner's endpoint.
Kick the receipt generation off the request thread — an @Async method on ReceiptService should do it.
Publish an OrderPlaced event to Kafka when the order is confirmed. Wire the producer.
Booking a trip reserves the flight, then the hotel, then charges the card. If the charge fails we have to unwind the first two. Design it.
An unpaid invoice should auto-cancel after 14 days. How do we hold that deadline?
New table for support tickets. What should the id column be — auto-increment or a UUID?
The mobile team wants the newest comments first. Just ORDER BY id DESC on the comments table, right?
Customers need an invoice number they can quote to support. Something like INV-2026-000123. Implement the generator.
Finance says our receipt numbers can't have holes in them. Make sure every number in the sequence gets used.
Add a Flyway migration for a customer_notes table and a repository method that loads notes for a customer.
This endpoint loads an order then loops over its lines fetching each product. Speed it up.
Add pagination to GET /customers. It returns everything right now.
Our 400 responses are just a string. Give the API a proper error body.
I can't tell why checkout is failing in prod. Add logging around the payment call.
Page someone when the order queue backs up. Add the metric and the alert.
Greenfield service, small team, mostly CRUD over Postgres with a few integrations. What should we build it in?
Two of the devs want to write the new reporting module in Go and keep it in this repo. Thoughts?
Set up CI for this repo. I want it to actually catch things, not just run tests.
SpotBugs is failing the build on 40 pre-existing findings. Can I baseline them and move on?
Add a library for working with public holidays and bump our dependencies while you're in there.
The build broke last week because something we depend on changed under us without us touching anything. Go through the Dockerfile and the workflow and make our builds reproducible.
Our orders service has grown to about 40k lines — billing, notifications and reporting all live in it. Should I split it into two, and where's the seam?
The partner API times out a lot. Add retries with backoff around the client.
Write a CLAUDE.md for this repo laying out how we want code written here.
Turn our style guide bullets into rules that the build can actually enforce.
We need a message broker. Compare the options properly and tell me which one, with reasons I can defend.
This ADR is from two years ago and nobody's checked it since. Is it still right?
Rename the variable `tmp2` in this snippet to something readable: `int tmp2 = a + b;`
What's the difference between `git rebase` and `git merge`?
Fix the typo in this Javadoc comment: `/** Retuns the customer name. */`
Write a regex that matches a UK postcode.
